input.question: Can a piece of toilet paper absorb the same amount of water after a cycle of wet-dry-wet?
input.ground_truth: Probably not. Toilet paper is designed to break up in water. I would expect the gaps in the fibers, the gaps that hold the water, would collapse as it soaks, leaving less volume for water retention after drying out.

response.prediction: After going through a wet-dry cycle, a piece of toilet paper cannot absorb the same amount of water as it did the first time. This is because toilet paper is made of cellulose fibers that swell and become less effective at soaking up water after they have been saturated and then dried. When the paper dries out, the fibers shrink and some of the spaces that held water before are no longer available. As a result, the next time you try to soak it up water, it will absorb much less than it did initially.
